subject: Delta-XL variant retrofit and telemetry gating
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ops@acmetech.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Delta-XL variant retrofit and telemetry gating

Team —

Quick heads-up: Acme (ops@acmetech.com) wants to adopt Delta-XL as a lower-cost variant for their realtime routing. Our staging runs show a subtle latency tail increase (~18th percentile) when key sequence lengths hit 2k+ and when batching crosses certain thresholds. Before we accept the onboarding request I want to formalize a short retrofit + telemetry gating plan so we can: 

- Surface exactly which kernel/codepaths are regressing
- Ensure we have the right prefix/KV telemetry to detect the tail in-prod
- Provide a targeted rollback/variant-switch matrix for their rollout window

Attachments: delta_xl_perf_summary.csv (staging perf dump), telemetry_spec.md (initial spec). Also linked a draft rollout matrix in Drive.

Ask: can infra (Karthik/Dev) assess whether this requires a model-side micro-optimization vs. serving config changes, and propose a minimal telemetry instrumentation that won't blow up ingestion? I want a short decision window (EOD today) so customer kickoff isn't blocked.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Product Manager, Model Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ops@acmetech.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta-XL variant retrofit and telemetry gating

+1 on the decision window. I skimmed the CSV — looks like the tail appears when batching merges two requests with large KV contexts. My initial take: we should attempt a serving-config-first path (batch-size cap + prefer-immediate flush for sequences > 1k) and add a lightweight telemetry key that tags requests with: model_variant, effective_batch_size, seq_len_bucket, and prefix_hit=true/false.

Concrete next steps from infra: 
- Dev: validate whether we can add the telemetry tags without a rolling restart (feature flag). If not, propose the strip-down flag set.
- I will draft a canary matrix that ties variant percentages to observed P99 and cost delta for Acme.

If the telemetry spec in telemetry_spec.md (attached) needs trimming to be safe w.r.t. PII, flag it.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Infrastructure

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta-XL variant retrofit and telemetry gating

Short update after local repro: the regression is correlated with kernel fallbacks when sequence length moves beyond the optimized attention tile (we're hitting a fallback path that is ~22% slower for long KV sequences). Two options:

A) Fast path (serving-config): cap batch size per-worker for requests with seq_len>1024 and enable immediate flush for prefix hits. Minimal risk, does not require new model artifact, can be rolled back instantly. Expected perf hit for small requests: <2%.

B) Medium effort (model + runtime): small model quantization/graph rewrite that keeps attention in the optimized tile. Requires new model package and compatibility gating (2–3 week timeline).

Telemetry: I can add the tags Karthik suggested behind a feature flag. That will require a short rolling restart unless we inject via a sidecar proxy (we can do sidecar + sampling for first 48 hrs). I recommend sidecar sampling at 10% for the first canary.

I'll attach a quick rollout matrix (rollout_matrix.xlsx) and a command list to flip the sidecar flags.

—Dev
Senior Engineer, Runtime

From: Alex Ramos <alex@openmodels.co>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta-XL variant retrofit and telemetry gating

Thanks for the notes — Alex from OpenModels (vendor) here. A couple clarifications from our side that might change prioritization: 
- The variant build Acme requested includes a slightly different tokenizer mapping for a legacy system; that increases effective token counts in some traces. If you see more sequences in the 1k–2k band, that could be why.
- We can ship a token-remap patch that reduces inflated token counts; low effort (1–2 days) but it requires a new model artifact and a pin window so we don't surprise other customers.

Happy to sync with Dev directly and coordinate pin windows. If you prefer, we can stage the token-remap in a compatibility mode that keeps previous token IDs as an alias for 7 days.

—Alex Ramos
Partner Eng, OpenModels

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acmetech.com, alex@openmodels.co
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta-XL variant retrofit and telemetry gating

Appreciate the quick turn. Decision summary and owners: 

- Short-term (canary day 0–3): apply Dev's serving-config (batch cap + immediate flush) + sidecar sampling at 10% for telemetry. Owner: Dev.
- Medium-term (day 4–14): ask OpenModels to provide token-remap patch staged as compatibility alias. Owner: Alex / OpenModels.
- Fallback: if P99 exceeds target for Acme during canary, immediately pin requests for Acme to Delta-XL-v1 (current stable) and hold onboarding. Owner: Karthik (automated routing policy).

Marissa — please create a short eval checklist (quality/regression prompts) we can run during canary and add the gating rows to JIRA-INF-4821. I'll upload the signed rollout_matrix.xlsx and link the Drive doc.

I'll block time for a 30-min sync first thing Monday to confirm rollout windows and customer comms. If anyone objects to the plan, reply here. Otherwise I'll mark this as the approved path and start the canary ticket.

Thanks,
Naomi
Product Manager, Model Ops
Redwood Inference
